We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $ρ\propto r^{-γ}$ with $γ\geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.

papers.title: New Universal Relations for Magnetized Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: Unlike the neutron-star mass--radius relation, which depends sensitively on the internal stellar structure through the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, certain neutron-star properties obey approximately universal relations that exhibit only weak dependence on the equation of state. In this paper, we explore new universal relations for magnetized neutron stars. We focus on a purely poloidal dipolar magnetic-field configuration and treat the effects of the magnetic field perturbatively to second order in the field strength. After appropriately normalizing the relevant quantities by the stellar mass and the magnetic-field strength at the pole, we first identify an exact universal relation between the magnetic dipole moment and stellar compactness. We then find approximate universal relations among the magnetic dipole moment, magnetically-induced stellar quadrupole moment, and ellipticity, with fractional variations due to the equation of state at the level of O(10%). We support these numerical findings with analytic estimates for Newtonian polytropes, which reproduce the observed behavior. Among the newly discovered relations, the one connecting the magnetic dipole moment and stellar quadrupole moment may be particularly useful for the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from binaries containing magnetized neutron stars.

papers.title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins
papers.abstract: We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can form rapidly spinning black holes, our central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks enabling efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the general expectation that black holes form with small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ code, $\texttt{CMC}$, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing ``significant'' events with mass ratio $q>0.1$. After identifying optimal candidates, we explore stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with $\texttt{MESA}$ models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, with roughly $10\%$ from ``significant'' mergers. Angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of $a\simeq 0.5$ or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.

papers.title: Tidal Deformability of Neutron Stars in Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences are valuable for testing theories of gravity in the strong field regime. By measuring neutron star tidal deformability using gravitational waves from binary neutron stars, stringent constraints were placed on the equation of state of matter at extreme densities. Tidal Love numbers in alternative theories of gravity may differ significantly from their general relativistic counterparts. Understanding exactly how the tidal Love numbers change will enable scientists to untangle physics beyond general relativity from the uncertainty in the equation of state measurement. In this work, we explicitly calculate the fully relativistic $l \geq 2$ tidal love numbers for neutron stars in scalar-tensor theories of gravitation. We use several realistic equations of state to explore how the mass, radius, and tidal deformability relations differ from those of general relativity. We find that tidal Love numbers and tidal deformabilities can differ significantly from those in general relativity in certain regimes. The electric tidal deformability can differ by $\sim 200\%$, and the magnetic tidal deformability differs by $\sim 300 \%$. These deviations occur at large compactnesses ($C = M/r \gtrsim 0.2$) and vary slightly depending on the equation of state. This difference suggests that using the tidal Love numbers from general relativity could lead to significant errors in tests of general relativity using the gravitational waves from binary neutron star and neutron-star--black-hole mergers.

papers.title: Rapid and robust simulation-based inference for kilonovae
papers.abstract: With the next generation of both electromagnetic and gravitational wave observatories beginning to come online, rapid analysis methods for kilonova data are becoming increasingly important in astronomy. Traditional Bayesian parameter estimation using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is time-consuming and relies on explicit likelihood approximations that can break down when modeling uncertainties are significant. We develop a simulation-based inference (SBI) framework for kilonova parameter estimation using density-estimation likelihood-free inference. The framework uses a Gaussian process emulator trained on $\sim 1300$ POSSIS simulations. We demonstrate that SBI provides a rapid alternative to MCMC that is robust to likelihood misspecification. The standard Gaussian likelihood approximation fails to capture the non-Gaussian, correlated structure of emulator uncertainty; SBI learns this structure directly from forward simulations. Simulation studies show that the SBI method accurately recovers injected parameters, while the MCMC suffers from systematic bias caused by likelihood misspecification. This problem persists when analyzing AT2017gfo, where a subset of the MCMC posteriors pile up at prior boundaries and the SBI posteriors do not. The SBI framework infers a total ejecta mass of $\sim 0.087 M_{\odot}$ dominated by lanthanide-poor ejecta and excludes toroidal and peanut ejecta geometries at the 99th percentile for both components. The SBI framework generates $\sim 2 \times 10^{4}$ posterior samples in seconds.

papers.title: Periodic Orbits of Van der Waals Black Holes
papers.abstract: Black holes in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime whose extended-phase-space thermodynamics reproduces that of a van der Waals fluid exactly form a distinctive class, the van der Waals black holes (VBHs). The timelike geodesics of VBHs are solved, their periodic orbits are catalogued, and the gravitational waves emitted along them are computed, so as to trace how the thermodynamic pressure P and the molecular-volume parameter b shape the orbital dynamics. Integrating the geodesic equations numerically yields the energy, angular momentum and radius of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and maps out the family of bound orbits. To delimit the parameter window in which the effective potential stays well behaved, we introduce a critical angular momentum Ls. Within the orbit-classification scheme, we compute the energies corresponding to rational q for several parameter sets and display the resulting orbits. The waveforms produced along these orbits are generated within the "Kludge" formalism, which makes it possible to quantify the imprint of b on the wave amplitude and on the period. Both the orbital architecture and the gravitational-wave signature turn out to be strongly sensitive to b. The dynamical behavior of VBHs and Schwarzschild-AdS (SAdS) black holes differs markedly, providing a new perspective for probing black hole thermodynamics via gravitational wave observations.

papers.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
papers.abstract: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

papers.title: On the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: Newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. To prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. However, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. In this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born PNS surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. We investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the CCSN that they stem from. We apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1D, 2D and 3D CCSN simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. In that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. More specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the PNS and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the PNS core and one near its surface. We also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the PNS, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. Our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the PNS properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.

papers.title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.

papers.title: Optical Geometry of a Lorentz-Violating BTZ-Like Black Hole: Reflection Double and Dirac Scattering
papers.abstract: We analyze the optical geometry of a static BTZ-like black-hole metric with a Lorentz-violating radial factor, distinguishing the one-sided black-hole exterior from the reflection double constructed from its optical spatial section. The optical metric is ultrastatic and has constant negative Gaussian curvature. The reflection double is smooth and complete, with a minimal circle; it is a geometric completion, not a demonstrated solution of the Einstein--bumblebee equations. We derive exact criteria for null-geodesic crossing and return, evaluate the corresponding angular sweeps, and determine the finite domain of a Euclidean surface-of-revolution embedding. Two inequivalent magnetic configurations are specified as external test fields on the embeddable patch. For a continuum graphene analogue on the doubled geometry, we derive the covariant massless Dirac operator and reduce its radial equation to Scarf-II partner equations. The full-line connection problem yields flux-normalized complex scattering amplitudes and probabilities, the resonance-pole lattice and its gamma-function residues, spectral widths and quality factors, the digamma Wigner delay, and conditional pole contributions to packet dynamics. We compare the analytic amplitudes with direct numerical integration of the radial partner equation, including their complex phases. We further separate fixed-$\ell$ from fixed-$Λ_e$ parameter protocols and audit the optical effective-mass degeneracy using Lorentzian curvature invariants, timelike geodesics, and a massive Klein--Gordon probe. Throughout, the gravitational completion, prescribed fields, and continuum scattering results are interpreted only within the scope of their respective constructions. Device-level graphene transport and a self-consistent gravitational wormhole require additional physical input.

papers.title: Axion cloud survival in nuclear star clusters
papers.abstract: Stellar perturbations can ionize a superradiant boson cloud while transferring energy and angular momentum from the perturbing orbits. We follow the cloud after superradiant saturation by coupling its occupation to a two-dimensional, orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation for the stars. The evolution includes stellar relaxation, capture, orbital backreaction, and gravitational-wave (GW) emission from both the cloud and the stellar orbits. We evolve 24 models with black hole masses $M=10^5$--$10^7M_{\odot}$ and couplings $0.04\leqα\leq0.40$. Stars with semimajor axes of a few Bohr radii, $r_c=M/α^2$, dominate ionization. Stellar replenishment from the outer cluster sustains ionization over hundreds of Myr, particularly for extended clouds. Of the 24 models, 21 lose at least $99\%$ of their initial cloud mass. For compact clouds, intrinsic GW emission dominates the depletion.

papers.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
papers.abstract: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $θ_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $ξ_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(ξ_{\rm pol}θ_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.

papers.title: Graviton Floor
papers.abstract: It has been observed that the Universe is permeated by the cosmic photon background, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. We investigate the conversion of the photon background into gravitons in the presence of background magnetic fields in the Milky Way Galaxy and in blazar jets. We find that the resulting graviton background is dominated by the contribution generated in blazar jets. Importantly, this graviton background constitutes a graviton floor for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors searching for new physics, analogous to the neutrino floor.

papers.title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract: Rotation weakens the radial instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in slow-rotation perturbation theory. We investigate its nonlinear effect by evolving stationary rotating drainholes supported by a phantom scalar field. We construct the backgrounds with an independent spectral solver, validate them against published symmetric solutions, and identify a misprint in a published field equation that did not affect the original authors' numerical results. Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy increases between the two spins compared. Second-order initial data excite the instability through their background truncation error. The results establish slower collapse and prolonged absence of detected radial growth for the sampled asymmetric backgrounds, over finite times from initially axisymmetric data.

papers.title: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
papers.abstract: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

papers.title: Landauer bound in a regular Bardeen black hole: extremality and evaporation
papers.abstract: Does the vanishing Hawking temperature of an extremal black hole imply that information can be erased without energy transfer? We investigate this question in the regular Bardeen geometry using a two-level quantum system, representing a quantum memory, coupled to a scalar bosonic field confined within an exterior cavity. The Hawking temperature tends to zero at extremality, as does the corresponding thermal Landauer scale. The field in an exterior cavity behaves differently, provided both walls remain away from the horizon, its lowest excitation energy stays finite. For a maximally mixed memory coupled to a reservoir initially in its unique ground state, we find $Q_\infty\geqΔ_{R,\infty}(1/2-ε)$, with $Δ_{R,\infty}$ the reservoir gap and $ε$ the reset error. For a resonant single-mode interaction, we give a reset protocol that attains the bound with no work supplied by the external control. In this example, the memory itself supplies the energy gained by the field. In the multimode calculation, counter-rotating terms are retained. Keeping the pulse parameters unchanged, we find a larger residual reset error closer to extremality. For reservoirs prepared thermally, we evaluate the Reeb--Wolf balance and find that the relative-entropy contribution, expressed in energy units, can have a finite low-temperature limit. These numerical preparations are externally imposed and remain hotter than the Hawking temperature. For comparison, an unconfined scalar field has near-extremal luminosity $P_\infty\propto y^4$, with $y=r_H/|g|-\sqrt2$. Assuming a particular quasistatic energy-loss prescription gives $y\propto t^{-1/2}$; this does not establish the existence of a stable remnant. For this particular reset operation, vanishing Hawking temperature therefore does not force the transferred heat to vanish.

papers.title: Primordial tensor mode from the neutrino sector
papers.abstract: We show that a regular solution for primordial tensor fluctuations can arise from the higher-order multipoles of the collisionless neutrino distribution after neutrino decoupling. Focusing on the leading case with the neutrino octupole mode (tensor-octupole mode), we derive the initial conditions for the Einstein-Boltzmann system and calculate angular power spectra for the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. Compared with the standard gravitational-wave mode, the tensor-octupole mode has a weaker large-scale metric response. It therefore gives a suppressed reionization bump and a different oscillation phase in the tensor CMB power spectra, providing a way to separate it from the standard tensor mode.

papers.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

papers.title: Set them free: extending RAMCOAL to model massive black hole triplets in hydrodynamical simulations of galaxies
papers.abstract: Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) and the higher-order multiples produced by repeated galaxy mergers evolve through regimes that cosmological simulations cannot resolve. These regimes determine merger delays, spins, recoils, and host galaxies at coalescence. We extend the RAMCOAL subgrid model to follow massive black hole triplets within hydrodynamical galaxy simulations. In the original three-stage binary model, black holes evolve as sink particles, undergo dynamical friction, and form bound binaries that harden through stellar scattering, gas torques, circumbinary-disc coupling, and gravitational-wave emission. When a hierarchical triplet becomes chaotic, RAMCOAL samples a library of outcomes from direct N body experiments and follows the resulting mergers, exchanges, and ejections alongside the accretion and spin evolution of each black hole. Isolated-galaxy tests with different triplet geometries show that orbital configuration alone can change which pair merges and its coalescence time. For the first time, we follow an MBH triplet to coalescence within a hydrodynamical simulation of gas-rich galaxies, coupling triplet-driven mergers to host-galaxy evolution. Subgrid integration costs less than 1 ms of single-core time per MBH system and time step, independently of particle resolution. The resulting coalescence properties reflect the environment encountered during subgrid evolution. RAMCOAL thus provides a step towards merger catalogues linking gravitational-wave signatures to the galaxies in which the black holes evolve.

papers.title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $μ_q$ and $μ_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordström black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $ω,k,T,μ_3\llμ_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $ω,k,μ_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
papers.abstract: The observation of over 300 Gravitational Wave (GW) events by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, has yielded information of the merger of compact object binaries, such as their individual masses and spins. However, the effective spin parameter obtained from the GW signal provides important information that could be used to discern the binary's formation channel. Overall, binaries formed from dynamic interactions in dense stellar environments are expected to have a random distribution of effective spins between -1 and 1. Meanwhile, binaries formed from the evolution of isolated stellar binaries are expected to have positive effective spins unless there is a large enough natal kick during the compact object formation that could significantly alter the orientation of the individual spins with respect to the binary's angular momentum. We study the viability of obtaining large natal kicks during the formation of massive Black Holes by studying the asymmetric mild explosion of $13\text{M}_{\odot}$, $21\text{M}_{\odot}$, $28\text{M}_{\odot}$ and $34\text{M}_{\odot}$ pre-supernova stellar models, by means of 3D Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics simulations. Our results show that, even kicks in the order of $\sim$ 1000 km/s, which are among the highest values observed for natal kicks, can't consistently change the orientation of the orbit. Physical setups where the orientation of the orbit changes require the kick to be directed correctly, and they would also require for the supernova explosion energy to be quite high.

papers.title: Magnetically Arrested Accretion and Black Hole Spin in a Semi-Analytic Model of Galaxy Formation
papers.abstract: We present {\sc Mad Sage}, a semi-analytic model of galaxy formation that couples black hole mass and spin evolution to gas accretion and AGN feedback under magnetically arrested disk conditions. Building on the {\sc Dark Sage} model, we incorporate GRMHD-calibrated prescriptions for spin evolution and jet power, spin-dependent radiative efficiencies, and remnant spins from BH-BH mergers. We compare accretion and feedback models, including coherent disk-fed accretion with mixed coherent and incoherent hot-halo accretion, with and without additional mechanical feedback. We find that incoherent accretion, together with Blandford-Znajek spin-down, drives massive BHs toward low spins, reducing jet efficiencies and weakening the quenching of massive galaxies. Reproducing the high-mass end of the stellar mass function requires either exclusively coherent accretion or an additional feedback component provided by ADAF outflows. Our models broadly reproduce observed BH-galaxy scaling relations, disk surface density profiles, and the AGN luminosity function at $z\sim 2-6$, although the spin models under-predict the number density of faint AGN at low redshift. At $z\lesssim 3$, predicted BH spins decrease with increasing BH mass, while at higher redshifts, the mass dependence weakens. Spin distributions peak at $|a_\star|\sim 0.5$-$0.7$, below current X-ray reflection spectroscopy measurements, and become bimodal for massive, quiescent BHs accessible with the next generation Event Horizon Telescope and the Black Hole EXplorer. We report that the predicted LISA event rates are nearly independent of the adopted accretion and spin models.

papers.title: Phentax: A JAX implementation of the IMRPhenomTHM waveform model
papers.abstract: The upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to be sensitive to thousands of white dwarf (WD) binaries in our galaxy, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of stellar-mass compact objects into massive black holes, stellar-mass black hole binaries (SOBHBs) in their early inspiral phase, and, crucially, massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with masses in the range of $10^4$-$10^7 M_\odot$. The presence of such a large number of signals requires joint inference of all parameters across all sources present in the data, an approach referred to as "global fit". This requires evaluating hundreds of thousands of waveform templates, which can be computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present $\texttt{Phentax}$, a $\texttt{JAX}$ re-implementation of the $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ waveform model. This is a state-of-the-art time-domain phenomenological waveform model for comparable-mass binary black holes that includes the effects of higher-order modes. Given this, $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ is one of the models currently used to simulate and analyze MBHB signals in LISA. With $\texttt{Phentax}$, we provide a fast, easy-to-batch, and differentiable implementation of this waveform model to accelerate the development of LISA global fit algorithms.

papers.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
papers.abstract: Physics beyond the Standard Model, whether of primordial or post-inflationary origin, can leave scale-dependent signals in the anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, we study how distinguishable these broad classes of signals are and quantify their level of degeneracy. In this initial investigation, for primordial features, we limit ourselves to those of the ``sharp'' and ``resonant'' kinds; for post-inflationary features, we consider two qualitatively distinct models: exotic energy injection, which deposits energy into the primordial plasma and modifies the global thermodynamic history, and early dark energy (EDE), which affects the CMB through the background expansion and gravitational perturbations. By studying representative examples, we find that while primordial features can leave oscillatory signatures in the CMB power spectrum with essentially arbitrary frequency and running, the post-inflationary models considered here produce qualitatively different patterns that cannot generically reproduce the characteristic running of primordial feature oscillations. We verify these findings first with a principal component analysis, and show using only the most significant principal components that there are no significant degeneracies between the primordial and post-inflationary features considered here, and secondly with a full likelihood analysis, which shows that the resulting posteriors do not change significantly when considering individual classes of models or combinations of primordial/post-inflationary features. While the two post-inflationary models probe distinct physical mechanisms and both are implemented in a simplified, phenomenological fashion, the methods used in this work can be generalized to include more realistic signals or other classes of signals.

papers.title: Optical Signatures of Sgr A* and M87* with Dark Matter Halos
papers.abstract: The event horizon telescope (EHT) has opened a new window onto the strong-field regime by imaging the shadows of the supermassive black holes (SMBHs) Sgr A* and M87*. These observations provide a unique laboratory for probing the dark matter (DM) distribution around black holes. In this work we systematically investigate the imprints of two distinct DM halo models, the cold DM (CDM), and the cored scalar field DM (SFDM) profiles on the gravitational lensing signatures of Sgr A* and M87*. We compute the photon spheres, shadows, weak and strong lensing observables, and caustic structures for both models. We then compared the obtained values of the shadow diameters with the EHT data, using $χ^2$ statistics. We found that all the models are within $1.2σ$ of the measured shadow diameters with the small $χ^2$ differences, $Δχ^2 \lesssim 1.2$. The caustic analysis reveals distinct topological regimes, Sgr A* retains both tangential and radial critical curves, while M87* may show only tangential critical curves due to its larger mass. This topological difference provides a clear observational signature for future observations.

papers.title: When Can Pulsar Timing Distinguish a Propagation Mass from a Weak Longitudinal Background?
papers.abstract: A weak longitudinal background can imitate the angular response of a gravitational-wave propagation mass. We quantify this ambiguity in a compressed Gaussian experiment constructed from the NANOGrav 15-year timing data. At a false-alarm probability of $10^{-3}$, allowing a weak longitudinal component in a massless background costs at least 16.29 percentage points of optimal rejection power for a specified source in a 20-pulsar subarray. Expanding the array to 40 pulsars at the same background level recovers at least 7.62 points. In a separate low-background experiment, we allow the same continuous range of longitudinal amplitudes at zero and positive mass. Across that range and three injected background levels, one test rejects zero mass with at least 97.38\% power at either of two masses separated by 1.08\%. With false assignment limited to $10^{-3}$ at the other mass, the power to identify either mass is at most 1.584\%. A cutoff can thus be identifiable before its position within a frequency cell can be resolved.

papers.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
papers.abstract: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Periodic flux modulations may arise from the orbital motion of black holes in close binaries, while relativistic jet precession can provide an additional source of periodic variability. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. For a total mass of $10^{8.95} M_\odot$ and a mass ratio q = 0.1, the derived milli-parsec separation and a short gravitational wave driven coalescence time, $t_c = 1122^{+144}_{-144}$ years, imply that PKS 0301-243 may be a rare source of nano-hertz gravitational waves and a potential multimessenger laboratory for the terminal stages of supermassive black hole coalescence.

papers.title: Leptogenesis with sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
papers.abstract: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.

papers.title: Nonconservative Lie series: post-Newtonian binary dynamics at 2.5PN
papers.abstract: We develop a Lie series perturbation method for solving the dynamics of nonconservative systems within the doubled phase-space Hamiltonian framework introduced in our previous work [PRE 113, 034137]. The procedure can be applied to a wide range of perturbed nonconservative systems which are not initially given by a Hamiltonian, by casting them into the doubled phase-space where the Lie method can be employed. As an application, we tackle the non-spinning $2.5$ post-Newtonian binary problem at leading dissipative order. Starting from the ADM radiation-reaction dynamics, we construct a resonant Birkhoff normal-form and the corresponding generator of the canonical transformation. Next, we establish an analytical perturbative solution accounting for both the long-term (secular) and short-term (oscillatory) temporal behavior, without performing a small-eccentricity expansion, for nondegenerate bound eccentric orbits. The secular piece is encoded in a resonant normal-form, and captures the long-term inspiral, reconstructing exactly the known Peters-Mathews relations for semi-major axis and eccentricity. The oscillatory piece completes the dynamics by supplying instantaneous, non-averaged corrections to the orbital parameters. Combined, the two pieces give a controlled, fully canonical description of the dissipative dynamics.

papers.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
papers.abstract: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.

papers.title: GradFlex: a Gradient-Based Method for Weak Lensing Flexion Measurement
papers.abstract: Flexion, the second-order gravitational lensing distortion, probes small-scale mass distribution and complement the cosmic shear measurement. However, its detection is highly challenging due to the faint signal and the contamination arising from the intrinsic galaxy morphology. In this Letter, we present GradFlex, a new method that extracts flexion from the gradient field of galaxy surface brightness distributions without assuming a specific point-spread function model or galaxy morphology. Using surface-brightness conservation, we relate the pre- and post-lensing gradient fields and derive flexion estimators from ensemble-averaged statistics of the corresponding spins. Tests on numerical simulations across diverse galaxy morphologies and multiple noise realizations demonstrate its reliability under realistic observing conditions. Combined with shear measurements, it could tighten constraints on cluster density profiles and enable more detailed studies of substructure than shear alone.

papers.title: Emulating the complex galactic-scale orbital dynamics of LISA massive black hole pairs with normalizing flows
papers.abstract: Massive black hole (MBH) pairs, formed in galaxy mergers, may coalesce in a burst of gravitational waves (GWs). Estimating the coalescence time-scales and rates is a long-standing astrophysical problem, essential to inform predictions for future GW detectors such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but remains challenging: MBH orbital decay in realistic galactic environments is complex and stochastic, and non-axisymmetric structures such as stellar bars can perturb MBH pair dynamics, delaying or accelerating binary formation and undermining the assumption that dynamical friction alone sets the inspiral duration. Capturing this evolution requires simulations too expensive to run at population scale. Here we present an artificial intelligence framework that emulates the galactic-scale orbital decay of an inspiralling MBH using conditional normalizing flows trained on a large suite of semi-analytical orbital integrations. Our model captures the evolution of secondary MBHs orbiting within multi-component galactic merger remnants featuring rotating stellar discs and bars, across a broad range of MBH masses, orbital configurations, and bar properties. The trained emulator reproduces the simulations' decay-time distributions while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude. For the first time, we apply this model to galaxy populations drawn from a cosmological simulation, exploiting morphological information on barred and non-barred galaxies to infer MBH binary formation time-scales across cosmic time. Our results show that stellar bars can alter the distribution of MBH binary formation times. More broadly, this demonstrates how simulation-based, surrogate machine learning emulators can unlock a class of astrophysical problems where the physics is well understood system-by-system but intractable at scale.

papers.title: Violent relaxation in hierarchical stellar systems: pathways toward massive black hole formation in the early Universe
papers.abstract: Massive stellar systems have been detected in the high-redshift Universe via the James Webb Space Telescope using gravitational lensing techniques. Such stellar systems may evolve on short dynamical timescales, despite a formally large 2-body relaxation time. If the stellar system consists of a large number of gravitationally bound clusters, a 2-body relaxation time can be defined for the star clusters in analogy to the 2-body relaxation time for stars, implying a faster evolution determined by the number of stars per cluster. At their formation, clusters will go through a process of "cold collapse" as part of their early, non-collisional, evolution. This phase enhances the mass segregation between the more massive and less massive population of stars. We derive a criteria based on the mass of the two components that determines under which conditions the massive component may even decouple from the cluster itself. Mergers of clusters and multiple mergers on average tend to produce systems with larger cluster radii. For the formation of massive black holes via dense stellar systems, the most promising pathway consists in the cold collapse of a dense massive cluster, after few mergers (or possibly none). In such a cluster with a sufficient number of massive stars, the massive population of stars will dynamically decouple in the central region and go through core collapse, leading to the formation of a central massive object. In the case of multiple mergers, massive but more spatially extended stellar systems will form.

papers.title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
papers.abstract: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbarω$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.

papers.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
papers.abstract: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe, as well as their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieve phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conduct a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters with broadly improved precision, some reported for the first time. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351 and J2043+1711, we determine their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and infer their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examine the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819 and J1741+1351, and estimate their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125-2327 and J1741+1351, we detect the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allows us to derive a strongly favored, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125-2327, and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we use the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar-timing-array analyses in the future.

papers.title: Lensing in the Blue III: Weak Lensing Shape Catalogs of 30 Merging Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present the weak gravitational lensing dataset from the Super-pressure Balloon-Borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT), which imaged 30 galaxy clusters during its 45 night flight in April to May 2023. SuperBIT is a first-of-its-kind balloon-borne imaging telescope that achieved near diffraction-limited observations in near-space conditions above 98% of the Earth's atmosphere. We use the metacalibration algorithm to obtain calibrated galaxy shapes for our target clusters and several calibration fields, enabling unbiased reconstruction of the weak-lensing signal. We employ several diagnostics throughout the pipeline, including assessments of point-spread function (PSF) modeling residuals and their impact on weak-lensing measurements, as well as tests for correlations between galaxy shapes and measured galaxy and PSF properties. To assess the multiplicative shear bias of the pipeline, we analyze a parallel set of simulated images that incorporate the real observing conditions from the flight, including measured SuperBIT PSFs, observed sky backgrounds, and detector noise, yielding a bias of $(1.54 \pm 6.00)$ per cent.

papers.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
papers.abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\simλ/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

papers.title: Reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 under the Goldilocks Prior
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from binary neutron star mergers encode the properties of the densest matter in the universe, but recovering them accurately requires controlling biases introduced by the inference framework. The recently developed Goldilocks Prior incorporates correlations predicted by a large ensemble of candidate equations of state and broadens them according to the expected detector sensitivity. We apply this framework to GW170817 and GW190425 and find that the inferred component tidal deformabilities differ substantially from standard analyses. For GW170817, we infer both neutron stars to be more tidally deformable than previously reported, with the most probable value for the lighter star nearly doubling from $Λ_2\simeq215$ to $Λ_2\simeq443$ relative to the uniform-prior analysis. For GW190425, the Goldilocks Prior considerably reduces the range of allowed tidal deformabilities. We propagate the resulting event likelihoods to the dense matter equation of state using two complementary hierarchical methods, a strongly parametrized spectral representation and a broader semi-parametric Gaussian-process ensemble. For GW170817, both prior treatments yield consistent EoS constraints despite substantial differences in the inferred properties of the individual neutron stars. For GW190425, however, the EoS constraints differ beyond numerical scatter even after removing the source-level priors, showing that prior choice affects likelihood recovery for low-SNR events. The joint EoS constraints nevertheless remain largely unchanged because GW170817 dominates the inference.

papers.title: X-ray Reflection as Diagnostic of Supermassive Black Hole Binary Properties
papers.abstract: We investigate correlations between prominent features in the relativistic X-ray reflection spectrum emitted by an accreting supermassive black hole (SMBH) binary with the underlying properties of the binary system. Model-independent measurements of the relativistic Fe K$α$ line ($\sim$6.4 keV) and the Compton reflection hump ($\sim$20-30 keV) are shown to be useful in constraining binary parameters. We compute 24,570 X-ray reflection spectra from two mini-disks attached to SMBHs at a fixed separation of 100 $GM/c^2$ on circular orbits, by varying its mass ratio, spin parameters, inclination, orbital phase and total mass accretion rate. We find that the location of the blue peak in the relativistic Fe K$α$ is a relatively robust diagnostic of the binary inclination, which could be obtained from a single-epoch X-ray spectrum. Given a few epochs of spectra, one may be able to determine the orbital phase of the binary and place constraints on its mass ratio by monitoring the Fe K$α$ centroid. Of all parameters, SMBH spin effects are most subtle and prone to measurement degeneracies. Some markers of high SMBH spin may nevertheless surface in the composite spectrum due to increased radiative efficiency. The approach developed here can be used to place preliminary constraints on binary parameters before a full parametrized X-ray spectral fitting method is available. It complements gravitational wave measurements by the Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) and the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna by providing independent constraints on binary parameters that may be prone to degeneracy (inclination), or otherwise inaccessible (spin for PTAs).

papers.title: Mixed Freeze-In and Freeze-Out Histories and Dark-Sector Decays in a $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Two-Scalar Model
papers.abstract: We study dark matter production in a renormalisable $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Higgs-portal model containing a complex scalar $S_A$ and a real scalar $S_B$, where one or both states remain out of thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model bath. We follow their coupled evolution through conversion, semi-annihilation, and the decay $S_B\to S_A S_A$ when kinematically allowed. We impose theoretical consistency conditions, limits on invisible Higgs decays, and LZ direct-detection bounds, accounting for each component's relic fraction. We check WIMP/FIMP assignments against interaction rates. When both states are stable, we find viable FIMP--FIMP and mixed WIMP--FIMP scenarios. In mixed cases, the WIMP-like state remains constrained by its Higgs-portal interactions, with the surviving points mainly concentrated near the Higgs resonance. The FIMP-like state can, however, provide a substantial fraction of the relic density with a negligible direct-detection signal. For $M_{S_B}>2M_{S_A}$, the decay of the heavier scalar leads to three production histories: SuperWIMP production, injection-assisted freeze-out, and sequential freeze-in. The mechanism depends on parent and daughter production. These decays can increase the abundance of a WIMP after freeze-out or contribute to the final abundance of a FIMP, changing the relation between the daughter's Higgs coupling and its relic density. Since the primary decays produce no Standard Model particles, electromagnetic and hadronic BBN bounds on visible decay products do not apply directly. We find $r_{\rm BBN}\ll1$ throughout the retained sample. To assess effects on structure formation, we use the dark matter fraction produced through decays and an equivalent thermal-WDM mass as approximate diagnostics. Some late-decay configurations are flagged as potentially warm, whereas the sequential freeze-in sample satisfies $m_{\rm WDM}^{\rm eq}\gtrsim1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

papers.title: A multi-epoch VLBI study of compact symmetric objects as contaminants in the search for milli-lenses
papers.abstract: The Lambda Cold Dark Matter model predicts a high abundance of low-mass dark matter halos, which can be probed through milliarcsecond-scale gravitational lensing (milli-lensing) of background radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The Search for MIlli-LEnses (SMILE) project aims to find these rare systems with Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). However, compact symmetric objects (CSOs) can closely resemble milli-lenses in VLBI images and are the main contaminant in such searches. We aim to determine the nature of the nine remaining milli-lens candidates of the SMILE pilot study and to characterize their physical properties. We analyzed all available multi-epoch, multi-frequency archival VLBI data, new HSA and EVN observations, and single-dish and connected-element interferometer measurements. We tested the lensing hypothesis through the morphology and spectra of the sources, and characterized their kinematics, spatially resolved spectral indices, magnetic fields, and integrated spectra, using synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) and free-free absorption (FFA) models. We identify eight of the nine candidates as CSOs, four of them for the first time. Spectral index asymmetries between components and previously undetected emission connecting them rule out the lensing hypothesis. Only J0923-3435 remains ambiguous. For the CSOs with known redshifts, the lobes have equipartition magnetic fields of $\sim$20-320 mG and projected separations of $\sim$60-240 pc, and show no measurable expansion, implying kinematic ages of at least $\sim$50-950 yr. The integrated spectra of J0210-2213 and J2347-1856 favor an inhomogeneous external free-free absorber over homogeneous and inhomogeneous SSA models. Since CSOs will be the main contaminant in the full SMILE survey, applying this framework will provide the same constraints for a much larger sample of compact radio-loud AGNs.

papers.title: Testing the Kerr hypothesis with orbital frequencies: lessons from spacelike singularities and black bounces
papers.abstract: The inner horizon of stationary black holes is subject to classical and semiclassical instabilities, suggesting that the Kerr interior should be modified. Quantum backreaction may drive the curvature to the Planck scale, producing a spacelike singularity, or halt its growth at lower curvatures, leading to a regular black bounce. We investigate the phenomenology of these two possibilities using, respectively, a Gürses--Gürsey geometry with a spacelike singularity and the rotating Simpson--Visser black bounce. Both geometries reproduce the light ring and ISCO frequencies of a Kerr black hole with the same ADM mass and angular momentum, by calibration in the first case and identically in the second. We find that the null and timelike convergence conditions are violated outside the horizon, up to a finite radius beyond the light ring in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and everywhere in the rotating Simpson--Visser spacetime. Moreover, their fundamental scalar quasinormal modes deviate from those of Kerr, most markedly in the damping, which is enhanced in the Gürses--Gürsey geometry and reduced in the rotating Simpson--Visser one. Thus, agreement with Kerr in a limited set of observables is not sufficient to establish the Kerr nature of a compact object, motivating complementary observational tests.

papers.title: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
papers.abstract: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.

papers.title: Magnetohydrodynamics During Reheating
papers.abstract: Reheating is a crucial phase that connects inflation with the hot Big Bang Universe. During this phase, the nonlinear interactions among the inflaton, the radiation plasma, and the primordial magnetic fields can influence the subsequent evolution of cosmic structures we observe today. In this paper, we develop a multifluid framework to investigate the evolution of three dimensional nonlinear magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) during the non instantaneous reheating phase driven by the perturbative decay of the inflaton into the radiation plasma. For the present paper, we consider the simplest scenario where the inflaton field homogeneously injects energy into the radiation sector. We study the MHD evolution of the coupled inflaton radiation system during the reheating phase, including the evolution of their individual kinetic energies, the velocity perturbations, vorticity, magnetic fields, and gravitational waves. We find that homogeneous energy transfer from the inflaton to the radiation sector increases the radiation and kinetic energy densities but does not significantly amplify the initial magnetic field perturbations. Consequently, the magnetic spectrum remains largely unchanged with respect to the instantaneous reheating scenario, while the velocity perturbations undergo a scale redistribution that affects the resulting GW spectrum. Our results demonstrate the importance of nonlinear multifluid MHD dynamics in understanding the evolution of primordial fields during reheating and provide a framework for exploring more realistic scenarios involving inhomogeneous decay processes and detailed thermalization effects.

papers.title: An ALMA sub-kiloparsec test of the Kennicutt--Schmidt relation in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at $z\sim2.78$
papers.abstract: [abridged] Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires resolving cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kpc scales. At z~2-3, near the peak of cosmic star formation, such resolution can generally only be achieved through strong gravitational lensing. We present an ALMA study of SMMJ0658, a 20x-magnified main-sequence star-forming galaxy at z=2.7768 +/- 0.0002, lensed by the Bullet Cluster (z=0.296) into three images. We use 0.2" and 0.6" ALMA Band-3 observations to test the Kennicutt-Schmidt (KS) relation at sub-kpc scales at cosmic noon. Using a JWST-based strong-lensing model of the Bullet Cluster, we reconstruct source-plane CO(3-2) and rest-frame 803um dust-continuum maps down to ~200pc scales. We derive spatially resolved molecular gas and star formation rate surface densities, depletion times, and the scale dependence of the CO-to-dust flux ratio over 200pc-3.2kpc apertures. The 0.2" ALMA data reveal massive, dense star-forming clumps, with Sigma_mol ~1.3-2.3 x 10^3 M_sun pc^-2, Sigma_SFR ~0.5-2.3 M_sun yr^-1 kpc^-2, and tau_dep ~0.82-2.56 Gyr. CO-dust spatial decorrelation produces a strong scale dependence in tau_dep. We find a KS-relation breakdown scale of 0.8 +/- 0.1 kpc, consistent with individual regions tracing distinct stages of the star-formation cycle. The ALMA and JWST data also reveal evidence for a lensed galaxy pair at z~2.78, although whether SMMJ0658 is undergoing an early-stage interaction remains uncertain. Our results show that the apparent universality of the KS relation breaks down once individual star-forming regions are spatially resolved, in line with observations from the local universe to z~1. We extend this picture to z~2.78, providing new insight into the resolved properties of the clumpy cold ISM and the star-formation cycle at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). Refining the strong lens sample with Space Warps crowd-sourced science
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the efficacy of crowd-sourced refinement of strong gravitational lens candidate samples by citizen scientists. Binary (lens/non-lens) classification by citizen scientists has been conducted previously, and here we extend such categorisation into `definite', `probable', `possible', and `non-lenses'. This grading is a required stage ahead of any strong lens sample publication and is usually carried out by (small) teams of researchers. We compare the responses of the volunteers to those of strong lens researchers and discuss the optimal strategy for lens classification and grading in future strong lens searches. Volunteers are found to be able to correctly identify systems of each grade, and their responses can be calibrated to be comparable to those of researchers. Grade posteriors, defined as the probability that a strong lens system classified by the volunteers is a certain grade, converge most rapidly for non-lens systems. We find that one researcher classification is equivalent to only 1.9 volunteer classifications when grading such systems. There is significant disagreement in the grading of intermediate-grade lens candidates amongst both volunteers and researchers. Moving towards calibrated lens probabilities for future lens searches would help to account for such subjectivity. If the Q1 lens search was rerun with volunteers performing lens grading (and corresponding calibration), a completeness of 79% for Grades A+B (corresponding to definite + probable lenses respectively) could be achieved with 41% purity prior to researcher inspection - this would correspond to an expected 12500 true lenses (i.e. excluding contaminants) in Euclid DR1.

papers.title: Metric reconstruction in a Bondi-like gauge
papers.abstract: Metric perturbations obtained from a Hertz potential in an ingoing radiation gauge (IRG) generically grow in an outgoing coordinate $r$ at future null infinity, and are therefore not asymptotically flat in the Bondi sense. Hollands and Toomani showed that this growth can be removed, within the Green--Hollands--Zimmerman (GHZ) framework, by an IRG-compatible ``residual'' gauge transformation together with a carefully chosen choice of the undetermined integration ``constants'' of the Hertz potential. In this work we turn that proof into a practical algorithm. We show that this entire completion is generated by a single ``Held Master Scalar'' (HMS), which can be thought of as a function on future null infinity. The HMS is obtained from the leading asymptotic piece of the $0$-Weyl scalar through a Teukolsky--Starobinsky inversion. We give explicit formulas for the four integration constants of the Hertz potential associated with the $0$-Weyl scalar, and for the residual gauge vector in terms of the HMS, thereby bringing the metric perturbation into a Bondi-like gauge. In Schwarzschild the entire construction is diagonal in $(\ell, m)$-modes and every completion field is available in closed form; in Kerr the construction is tri-diagonal. We have numerically implemented the full scheme in $(\ell,m)$ and in $m$-modes, including the corrector piece of the GHZ framework. We illustrate our scheme numerically for a point-particle on a circular orbit in a puncture scheme in Schwarzschild and in Kerr, by demonstrating the Bondi-like fall-off. We also find agreement with the known Detweiler redshift computations in Schwarzschild and Kerr. Our method directly gives the Bondi news, mass-, and angular momentum aspects, for which we give exemplary results in Kerr.

papers.title: A new era for Dual AGN science with SHARP
papers.abstract: The search for and the characterization of ultra-compact dual active galactic nuclei (AGN) are among the hottest topics of current extragalactic astrophysics. These systems involve two accreting massive black holes (MBHs) embedded within the same host galaxy, with relative projected separations from a few hundred pc down to a few pc. They are central to understanding hierarchical galaxy formation, black hole growth and demographics, and accretion-feedback coupling in the most extreme interaction phases. Even more compellingly, such tight pairs are the most direct precursors of gravitationally bound binary MBHs (sub-pc scale separation), which are among the loudest emitters of gravitational waves (GWs) in the low-frequency ranges. SHARP will deliver the first statistical census and physical characterization of ultra-compact dual AGN up to cosmic distances, finally bridging the observational gap between kpc-scale pairs and sub-pc GW-emitting binaries, and enabling a breakthrough understanding of MBH growth, feedback and co-evolution across cosmic time.

papers.title: Grey-body factors of black holes
papers.abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behavior in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.

papers.title: Observational Test of the Maximum-Entropy Conjecture for Black-Hole Mergers with GW250114
papers.abstract: The remnants of binary black-hole (BBH) mergers are accurately described by numerical relativity, but the physical principle governing the selection of the final states remains unclear. A recently proposed maximum-entropy conjecture suggests that a BBH merger produces the Kerr BH that maximizes the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, subject to the post-Newtonian formalism or balance laws for energy and angular momentum. In this work, we test this conjecture with the event GW250114, inferring the progenitor and remnant properties from the observed pre-merge and post-merge signals, separately. We construct the surrogate Kerr entropy associated with candidate remnant states along the inferred energy-angular-momentum trajectory. We then compare the maximum-entropy state with the independently inferred mass and dimensionless spin of the final BH. We find that the conjecture predicts a remnant mass of $M_f=70.0^{+0.35}_{-0.21}\,M_\odot$ and spin of $χ_f=0.70^{+0.00}_{-0.01}$, compared with the ringdown estimates $M_f={72.3}^{+3.6}_{-3.7}\,M_\odot$ and $χ_f=0.74^{+0.05}_{-0.07}$. The entropy deviation is consistent with zero within the $68\%$ credible interval for our fiducial analysis, and variations in the pre-merger truncation time and quasi-normal modes (QNM) content reveal no compelling discrepancy with the conjecture.

papers.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
papers.abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.

papers.title: On the Detectability of Compact Multi-Planet Systems via Gravitational Microlensing
papers.abstract: Compact multi-planet systems orbiting ultracool dwarfs, such as TRAPPIST-1, may be a major population of terrestrial worlds with poorly constrained demographics. Individual close-in planets are expected to escape microlensing detection, but whether a compact system can produce a detectable collective signal remains to be quantified. We calculate the microlensing signal from each TRAPPIST-1 planet, and of all seven combined, if the system were a lens toward the bulge. For a 0.09 $M_\odot$ lens at 4 kpc, $R_E \approx 1.21$ AU, placing the planets at $s = 0.010$--$0.051~θ_E$, 12--63 times interior to the lensing zone. We measure each signal as the residual after fitting a single-lens model, which accounts for the barycentric dipole. Because the quadrupole term cancels between the two images to first order, the residual scales as the octupole ($q s^3$), reaching $|δA / A| \sim 10^{-6}$.
